title: RTL-aware layout with logical properties
description: A layout approach that works in both left-to-right and right-to-left languages: CSS logical properties (inline-start/end, block-start/end) instead of left/right, the dir attribute set per document and per embedded content, mirrored directional icons, and isolation of mixed-direction text such as names and numbers.
intent: Ship one layout that reads correctly in Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, and Urdu as well as LTR languages, without a separate stylesheet.
characteristics: margin-inline, padding-inline, inset-inline, text-align: start everywhere
dir on html plus dir="auto" or bdi for user-generated content
directional icons (arrows, chevrons) mirrored; others (play, check) not
numbers, code, and phone numbers isolated
layouts tested in both directions in CI
interaction: Swipe and carousel directions follow reading direction; keyboard arrows in horizontal widgets follow visual direction.
responsive: Logical properties apply at all breakpoints; check that off-canvas drawers open from the inline-start side.
accessibility: Correct lang and dir attributes so screen readers pick the right voice; do not mirror text by transform; ensure focus order follows visual order in both directions.
limitations: Third-party widgets may hardcode left/right and need overrides.
Fonts must cover the target scripts; typographic scale often needs adjusting for Arabic script.
